question: Is 4+2 still the best segmentation under the deployed rule (DG + answer check), and would it be chosen on data it is not reported on?

rules.joint: block iff DG > eta and (ADL > eta_A or Echo >= 1); supp_rules.joint_thresholds on judgeable benign rows
rules.dg: block iff DG > eta; eta = benign 95% quantile (judgeable rows)

conventions.br_effective: unjudgeable attacks counted as blocked (fail-closed miss)
conventions.br_poisoned: blocked or unjudgeable / attacks whose cached answer is poisoned (supplementary: the answer check exists to pass unpoisoned ones)
conventions.fpr_effective: unjudgeable benign rows counted as blocked
conventions.asr: mean(cos>=0.90 AND poisoned AND served) over all attack rows; unjudgeable rows are not served; cos from the row tables
conventions.cost_rel: mean stored span variants per judgeable row / 4+2, geometric mean over CAP/SCP/KCA (fig7_tradeoff_ranked.py)
conventions.eligibility: rq3_selection_split.eligible_cells: benign rows unjudgeable at 3 segments <= 1% in every corpus
conventions.benign_pools: CAP and SCP share the 499 ComQA benign rows; KCA uses 499 NQ rows
conventions.bootstrap: 2000 intent-grouped replicates, benign intents per pool and attack intents per class, thresholds refit
conventions.selection: one 50/50 split of the union of intent_ids per seed (np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle, as rq3_selection_split.py), shared by all classes; thresholds and choice from the selection half only; the test half reads the selection-half thresholds unchanged; ties at the top broken by lower selection-half cost
